Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the run chase! The umpires and the players of Australia Women are back out in the middle. It will be the pairing of Danni Wyatt-Hodge and Maia Bouchier to open the innings for England Women. Megan Schutt will start proceedings with the ball. Let's go...
... The Run Chase ...

Right then, 186 is what England Women need to get their first win of the series and still have a shot at drawing the 2025 Women's Ashes. They have beaten Australia Women 4 out of 5 times at the ground but it won't be an easy chase. Australia Women will look to seal the Ashes with the ball and it should be an entertaining watch. Stay tuned as the run chase is up next.

There was a lot of talk before the game about the athleticism or the lack of it from England Women shown in this series by their former player Alex Hartley to which Amy Jones gave a cold answer. However, the dropped catches and a few lapses in fielding do once again bring up that question. They bowled well in the middle phase of the innings with Sophie Ecclestone and Charlie Dean really ruling the roost but let it slip at the death and once again Sarah Glenn was hit away for plenty of runs.

After being inserted into bat, Australia Women started positively as Beth Mooney yet again used her feet to good use and mustered up quick boundaries inside the Powerplay. However, Georgia Voll got run out and that triggered a bit of a collapse after the Powerplay and soon enough, Australi were 4 down for 70 odd runs. Tahlia McGrath and Annabel Sutherland countered well and got the hosts back on track before McGarth and Grace Harris just went berserk at the death to propel Australi to 185 runs.

That was some acceleration from Australia Women in the death overs and they picked up 48 runs in the last 3 overs to put on another big total on the board thanks to stellar hitting from Tahlia McGrath and Grace Harris. England Women on the other hand have failed to capitalize on opportunities once again and are under the pump now.

Excellent running! Slower ball, pitched up outside off, Grace Harris waits well and drives it firmly and just wide of Freya Kemp at long on. They push hard for two and it is a tired-looking throw from Kemp towards the keeper's end and Australia Women finish with 185/5 on the board!

TOSS - The flip of the coin lands in favor of England Women and they will BOWL first.

Right then, it is forecasted to be a cloudy evening in Canberra with some chance of precipitation later on as well but the weather should stay dry for most parts of the game. A very crucial contest on the cards, especially for England Women who continue their search for a first win in this series. Will they get the job done here? Or will Australia Women yet again prove to be clinical enough and take an unassailable 10-0 lead in the Ashes? We shall find out. Toss and team news in bit, so, stick around.

England Women have blown hot and cold in all four matches so far in the Women's Ashes and have just failed to capitalize on opportunities and with Maia Bouchier really struggling at the top of the order, they have found themselves in early trouble every time. Sophia Dunkley though returned to the side and scored a stellar half-century but they need more individuals to stand up and deliver when required. Even their highly-rated spin trio of Sophie Ecclestone, Charlie Dean and Sarah Glenn underperformed last time around but they do have the players that can beat this Aussie side.

Australia Women sealed the three-match ODI series with a clean sweep and have begun the T20I leg of the Women's Ashes with another commanding victory. With skipper Alyssa Healy and Ash Gardner both missing out in the first game, the Aussies flexed their depth and we might see at least Healy sitting this game out as well. The debutant Georgia Voll impressed last time around and she might get another go here alongside Beth Mooney who really set the tone in that first inning.

Hello and a warm welcome to the Manuka Oval in Canberra for the 2nd T20I of the Women's Ashes between Australia Women and England Women. With the Ashes retained, the Aussies will now look to win the multi-format series outright today. England are down 8-0 in the series with as many as 8 more points up for grabs and this now becomes a must-win game if they are to draw the series.
... MATCH DAY ...

The 2025 Women's Ashes series has proven to be overwhelmingly dominated by Australia, despite being one of cricket's most anticipated rivalries. With an unassailable 8-0 lead in the points, Australia has retained the prestigious trophy for the third consecutive time, showcasing their supremacy across formats. Their path to victory included a commanding 3-0 sweep in the ODIs, followed by continued success in the T20I segment. What makes Australia's performance particularly remarkable is their ability to maintain such high standards despite notable absences. The team is competing without Ashleigh Gardner due to injury, and captain Alyssa Healy will be unavailable for the upcoming Test match. However, their depth has proved more than adequate to overcome these setbacks. In the batting department, Beth Mooney's outstanding performance in the first T20I, well supported by debutant Georgia Voll, exemplified their batting prowess. While star all-rounder Ellyse Perry has had a quiet series thus far, the team's batting depth has effectively covered for her temporary form dip. Tahlia McGrath's return to form has been another positive development, showing signs of overcoming her recent inconsistency. The bowling unit has been equally impressive, with spinners Wareham and King leading the attack with their crafty variations, while pace bowlers Schutt, Sutherland and Garth have provided valuable support. But what has went wrong with the English side? A telling statistic reveals that in all four white-ball matches played so far – both in ODIs and the first T20I – the English team has failed to bat out their full quota of overs. While there have been moments of resistance against the dominant Australian side, these efforts have proven insufficient due to a lack of consistency. Sophia Dunkley has shown glimpses of fight with the bat, but her dismissals have often triggered dramatic collapses. More worryingly, established players like Natalie Sciver-Brunt, Heather Knight, and Danni Wyatt-Hodge have struggled to make significant impacts. The batting statistics paint a stark picture, with wicketkeeper-batter Amy Jones being the only English player to accumulate more than 100 runs in the series so far, despite batting in the lower middle order. With the crucial Test match approaching, England desperately needs these experienced players to rediscover their form. In the bowling department, Sophie Ecclestone has maintained her high standards, but has lacked consistent support from her fellow bowlers. However, the broader issue remains that even strong bowling performances are being undermined by the team's batting struggles, highlighting the need for a more balanced team performance. As the Women's Ashes moves to Canberra's Manuka Oval for the second T20I, England faces a critical moment in the series. While the Ashes trophy may be out of reach, they still have pride to play for and an opportunity to claim the T20I series by winning both remaining matches. Meanwhile, Australia enters the contest looking to extend their winning streak to five consecutive games. Whether England manages to mount a comeback or Australia continues their dominant run, cricket fans can look forward to another exciting chapter in this series.
